text: 各位同学,大家好,我是来自上海市三星学校的陈妍。I'm happy to see you again.In today's lesson, we are going to learn about New Year food traditions.Before we start our lesson,Please get your student's book, worksheet, and pen ready.Let's start.Boys and girls, we know during Chinese New Year, people have a long list of things to do.For example, people enjoy the traditional food.What New Year food traditions do you know?People eat spring rolls in Chinese New Year.People in Northern China eat 饺子 on Chinese New Year's Eve.People eat fish for Chinese New Year's Eve dinner.Great!You know many New Year food traditions.Why do people have these food traditions?Let me take fish as an example.The Chinese word for fish, 鱼, sounds like the word for surplus, 鱼.People believe eating fish will bring wealth and luck for the New Year.人们相信吃鱼会给新的一年带来财富和好运。Today, we are going to read about New Year food traditions in different cultures.Please take a look at the pictures and subheadings.What food can we find from the text?Zoe, what's your answer?Tangyuan, Toshikoshi soba and 12 grapes.Right!Toshikoshi soba means 跨年草麦面 in Chinese.Do you know anything about them?Lily, any idea?People eat tangyuan during Chinese New Year.It's round shape means family members are together and happy.What about Toshikoshi soba and 12 grapes?Maybe you have no idea.Never mind.I'd like to know what you want to know about these New Year food traditions.I want to know why people eat these foods in the New Year.Which country or area can people find these food traditions?How long have these traditions been around?Thank you.You raised many questions.I'm glad you are interested in these food traditions.Now, please read the text and take the information you can find from it.It tasks one in your worksheet.Time's up.Let's check.Lily, what's your answer?We can find out why people eat these foods in the New Year, in which country or area people can find these food traditions, and when people eat these foods.You are right.Do you have the same answer?I hope so.Now, let's find out the answers to these questions.Please read the text carefully and complete the table.It's task two in your worksheet.In which country or area do people eat tangyuan?Emma, what's your answer?In southern China.在中国南方。When do people eat tangyuan?They eat it for breakfast on the first day of Chinese New Year.Exactly.Why do people eat tangyuan?Lucas, what's your answer?To show a wish for the unity and happiness of the whole family.Yes, unity means 和谐和睦 in Chinese.Good job.You've got all the information about tangyuan.What about toshikoshi soba?Grace, what information have you found?People in Japan usually eat toshikoshi soba on New Year's Eve to wish for a long life and good luck in the New Year.Do we Chinese eat noodles to wish for a long life?Danny, you please.Yes, we also have the food tradition of eating noodles.What's the difference between these two food traditions?We eat noodles to wish for a long life on our birthdays, not on New Year's Eve.What about twelve grapes?Peter, please share the information you've found.People in Spain and Latin America eat twelve grapes at midnight on New Year's Eve to wish for good luck every month next year.Excellent.Here, Spain means 西班牙 and Latin America means 拉丁美洲.Twelve months, twelve grapes.Twelve grapes means people will have a whole year of luck.We've read about three New Year food traditions.Which food tradition do you find the most interesting and why?Think about it.Lucy, what's your idea?I think eating twelve grapes at midnight on New Year's Eve is the most interesting one.I like grapes and grapes are common.But I never eat grapes at midnight.Each grape means a month of luck next year.It's fun and special.If I can get twelve grapes into my mouth, all of my wishes will come true.Thanks for sharing, Lucy.As we can see, people from different cultures welcome the New Year with different food traditions.What do these New Year food traditions have in common?这些新年饮食传统有什么共同之处?Please think it over.Thank you for watching.Grace, please share your opinion with us.Good answer.I agree with you.Do you still remember the big question of Unit 3?What role does food play in our life?After reading this text,what's your answer?Lucas, you please.I think food can carry special meanings,such as good luck and long life.We can say people around the worlduse food to express their wishes.We can say people around the worlduse food to express their wishes for the future.Peter, any idea?I think food can help us learn about different cultures.Each culture has its own special dishes and food traditions.When we try food from another culture,we are learning about their way of life,their celebrations, and their values.I agree.Food is a big part of every culture.It can help us explore different cultures.Boys and girls,we've talked about many New Year food traditions so far.I'd like to know what New Year food traditionsyour family follow.Linda, any idea?My family eat Nian Gao.It's a wish to be successful and higher each year.This year will be better than the last.Thanks for sharing, Linda.I guess you eat Nian Gao on the first day of Chinese New Year.People hope their lives will be better and better every year.Zhouyi, please share your answer with us.My family eat Jiaozi when we are having Chinese New Year's Eve dinner.Jiaozi look like yuanbao.We believe eating them will bring us wealth and luck in the New Year.Thanks for sharing,Zhouyi.Your hometown must be in the north of China.When we introduce the Chinese New Year food tradition,remember to introduce the name of the food.Which region has or which regions have this food tradition.When people eat the food and why people eat the food.Now it's time for you to introduce one Chinese New Year food traditionyour family follow.You have one minute to prepare.Let your food be a food tradition.Lily, can I have a try?Families in most parts of China eat fish for New Year's Eve dinner.The Chinese word for fish sounds like the word for surplus in Chinese.When people have fish, they usually say 年年有余。They hope they will have a surplus of food and money in the coming year.Boys and girls, how do you like Lily's introduction?Did she mention the name of the food?Did she mention which region has or which regions have this food tradition?Did she mention when people eat the food?Did she talk about why people eat the food?Lily's introduction is very detailed.I believe all of you did a great job.This is your homework.Read the text aloud on page 52, Student's Book 6A, after the recording, until you can read it very fluently.Write an introduction to one of the Chinese New Year food traditions in at least 50 words.Search the Internet to learn about at least two New Year food traditions in different cultures and take notes in the table.That's all for today's class.See you next time.
